name: Workflow Machine

hlido_opinion.headline: A describe-it-and-we-build-it automation tool with refreshingly transparent pricing — a cleaner on-ramp than Zapier/n8n for AI-assisted workflows, if it can prove reliability at scale.
hlido_opinion.body: Workflow Machine's pitch is 'stop building workflows, start describing' — you tell it what to automate in natural language and it assembles the trigger/condition/action blocks. What lifts it above the crowded automation space on the public surface is not the AI framing (everyone has that now) but two concrete things: transparent, self-serve pricing published right on the page (Free / $18 / $48, with explicit run counts, AI-credit allowances, active-workflow limits, run-record retention, and per-run time caps), and an honest emphasis on operability — visible workflow steps, expression-based logic without dropping to code, sample-data testing, execution logs, retries, and per-run inspection. That combination signals a team that understands the real pain of automation isn't building the happy path, it's debugging the failures. The integrations named (Slack, Gmail, Postmark, Google Docs/Slides/Tasks, OneDrive) are the standard business set. The honest caveats: this is a young product in a category with deeply entrenched incumbents (Zapier, Make, n8n), Hlido saw no third-party traction or trust signals on the surface, and reliability/quality were not tested hands-on. But transparent pricing plus an operability-first framing is a credible, buyer-respecting position.

tier_rationale: STEADY (72) primarily because the pricing is fully transparent and self-serve (a real Value-Signal strength), the product is coherent, and the framing emphasises the operability features (logs, retries, testing, inspection) that make automation actually usable. Held at low-STEADY because it competes against entrenched incumbents, shows no third-party traction on the surface, and was not tested hands-on — confidence is medium.
what_it_does_well: Fully transparent, self-serve pricing with explicit limits (runs, AI credits, workflows, retention, per-run time)
Operability-first: visible steps, execution logs, retries, sample-data testing, per-run inspection
Natural-language 'describe it and we build it' on-ramp lowers the setup barrier
Standard business integrations out of the box (Slack, Gmail, Google Workspace, OneDrive, Postmark)
Reusable templates and expression-based logic without forcing custom code
what_it_fails_at: Crowded category with entrenched incumbents (Zapier, Make, n8n) — differentiation is thin beyond the NL on-ramp
No third-party traction, customer references, or trust signals visible on the public surface
Reliability, retry behaviour, and AI-build accuracy were not tested hands-on
Free-tier limits (100 runs, 2 active workflows, 15-min poll) are tight for anything beyond evaluation
Integration breadth is standard, not distinctively deep
best_for: Freelancers and small teams wanting AI-assisted automation without learning a node editor
Buyers who value transparent, self-serve pricing over 'contact sales'
Lead-management, support, and content workflows across common SaaS apps
not_recommended_for: Enterprises needing proven scale, SLAs, and a deep integration catalogue
Teams already invested in a mature automation platform without a clear reason to switch
Mission-critical workflows that need independently verified reliability first

evidence_urls.claim: Describe workflows in natural language and the product builds them
Transparent self-serve pricing: Free / $18 / $48 with explicit run and workflow limits
Execution logs, retries, sample-data testing, and per-run inspection
Built-in integrations (Slack, Gmail, Postmark, Google Docs/Slides/Tasks, OneDrive)

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: Positioned as 'automation for you and your AI agents' — workflows are triggered by events/integrations and can sit downstream of an agent, but the primary surface is a web builder rather than a programmable API/CLI/MCP interface. Webhook/trigger integration inferred from the integrations and trigger-block model; not exercised.

checklist.evidence: Transparent Free/$18/$48 tiers with explicit limits shown on page
Use-case examples (lead management, support, content, research, data) + FAQ; no live demo tested

summary: A describe-it-and-we-build-it automation tool with refreshingly transparent pricing — a cleaner on-ramp than Zapier/n8n for AI-assisted workflows, if it can prove reliability at scale.
